proposal.title: Aurelia vendor variants — printers specialist
proposal.reason: Apply the author's vendor-owned/vendor-sold cooperation model and inclusive midpoint >=70% rule. Probabilities are subjective scenario judgments, not historical observations or shipment guarantees. Logix provides design help and AION may supply chips; no OEM-only supply to Logix, Logix ownership or Logix resale is assumed. Preserve historical records and add linked, separately dated scenario offerings. Qume Sprint 5/45 RO — Aurelia-compatible variant: 75–90%, midpoint 82.5%, estimated release 1980-03. Diablo 1610 — Aurelia-compatible package: 65–80%, midpoint 72.5%, estimated release 1980-05. NEC Spinwriter 5510 — Aurelia-compatible package: 70–85%, midpoint 77.5%, estimated release 1980-05. Comprint 912 — Aurelia-compatible package: 65–80%, midpoint 72.5%, estimated release 1980-04. Heath H14 — Aurelia-compatible kit: 60–80%, midpoint 70%, estimated release 1980-04. SWTPC PR-40 — Aurelia-compatible variant: 60–80%, midpoint 70%, estimated release 1980-04. Full reassessment and release basis: data_storytelling/review_evidence/aurelia-vendor-variants/assessment.json and offerings.json.

specification.description: Alternative-history Aurelia offering derived from {source_1}. {vendor} owns, manufactures, brands, sells and supports the finished product. Logix may assist with design and AION Labs may supply necessary chips and ROMs; neither becomes the finished-product owner or seller. The direct release date is an estimated scenario month, not a historical release claim. Existing source products keep their original identities and interfaces.
Qume sells a receive-only daisywheel printer with a FlexiBUS interface option. The controller provides bounded buffering and reports only status signals actually supported by the printer.

The vendor implements FlexiBUS discovery, differential serial transport, framing, bounded requests/retries and flow control using Logix design assistance and AION-supplied interface components where needed. One device connects to each host port; this product supplies no implicit hub or daisy chain. Attach only while the port is quiescent. The peripheral has its own power supply unless the qualified keyboard power budget applies. Vendor-supplied Aurelia Z80/CP/M software handles this device; no arbitrary firmware auto-execution, cross-CPU binary compatibility or later networking/pointer support is implied.

The existing printer class provides bounded output and status. Native print-language and graphics features remain vendor-specific. Report only available status and distinguish accepted data from physically completed output.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Alternative-history assessment at the estimated release month of this vendor-owned and vendor-sold Aurelia offering. The scenario assumes the described implementation and host integration are delivered; the date is not historical shipment evidence.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Implements the FlexiBUS transport and the existing printer device contract.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Adds a vendor-owned Aurelia peripheral path and increases the usefulness of FlexiBUS. This does not imply Logix ownership, exclusive distribution or a measured sales multiplier.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Alternative-history assessment at the estimated release month of this vendor-owned and vendor-sold Aurelia offering. The scenario assumes the described implementation and host integration are delivered; the date is not historical shipment evidence.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The vendor supplies the stated peripheral and compatible host integration for the Aurelia platform, including its monochrome configuration. Any narrower display mode or software requirement is stated in the specification.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: Expands what an Aurelia owner can purchase from an independent supplier; vendor ownership and sales remain separate from Logix.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Alternative-history assessment at the estimated release month of this vendor-owned and vendor-sold Aurelia offering. The scenario assumes the described implementation and host integration are delivered; the date is not historical shipment evidence.
impacted_products.comparison_description: This independently sold compatible offering is an alternative purchase in the same peripheral role, within the stated feature and configuration differences.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: Can take sales from the Logix offering while strengthening the shared ecosystem; cooperation does not eliminate product competition.

specification.description: Receive-only daisywheel printer, approximately 45 characters/s. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Assess {historical_product} in its recorded {host} configuration. Compare usable printer configurations with their actual interface, driver, paper and output requirements.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Parallel/serial printing is not FlexiBUS. A bridge would need device identification, status mapping, backpressure and protection against duplicate output after uncertain retries. The relationship concerns alternative complete configurations, not proven direct compatibility with this standard.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: A broad established printer choice can weaken the incentive to adopt a bus with a narrower qualified range. A validated bridge could broaden that range, but neither a bridge delivery nor higher sales is assumed.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. Receive-only daisywheel printer, approximately 45 characters/s.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative combines the MPI MP40 mechanism with a FlexiBUS device controller. Compare actual print width, character repertoire, quality, paper handling and qualified driver support; the current definition establishes no universal speed or output-quality advantage. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: The printer is an alternative hardcopy purchase where the host supplies its required interface and driver. Width, output quality, throughput and consumables can favour it for different jobs; it cannot connect directly to FlexiBUS. This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.
